title: Iris, Messenger of the Gods
description: Rodin turns a dancer’s extended leg and arched torso into a forceful image of flight. The bronze fragment depicts the mythological messenger Iris. The scanned cast was lent by Iris Cantor for Portland Art Museum’s 2017 Rodin exhibition.
adult_art_context: Portland museum label identifies a female figure probably modeled from a can-can dancer. Historical adult nude sculpture with exposed anatomy and an acrobatic pose; no sexual act. Present in upright whole-sculpture museum view rather than genital detail.
secondary_license_note: Cults text extraction did not show a license label. Original Thingiverse license must be verified independently.
artwork_rights: Rodin composition modeled in 1891; artist died in 1917. The scanned bronze cast date is unknown. The separate 3D scan is licensed CC BY 4.0.
attribution: Iris, Messenger of the Gods, Auguste Rodin, modeled 1891, bronze, Georges Rudier Foundry (cast date unknown). Lent by Iris Cantor to Portland Art Museum, 2017. 3D scan by Adam McGee (WWWdotPDXDDDdotCOM / Portland 3D LLC), via Thingiverse, CC BY 4.0; processed by Atrium.
